candidate.hyperbolic_necessity: Negative curvature is a falsifiable design hypothesis, not a conclusion from the evidence. The observed transitions are directed in aggregate, while literature identifies shared-prefix preference rank reversals as a concrete next-item expressiveness failure. Negative curvature may allocate more representational separation to branching directions at increasing residual depth, potentially allowing similarly embedded items with different transition neighborhoods to receive distinct two-token prefixes. Neither the transition statistics nor the cited literature prove this geometry is necessary; failure to improve registered diagnostics or Stage3 behavior rejects the hypothesis.

math_definition.architecture: For each item i, a frozen-protocol content encoder produces z_i in R^32. Quantize it with three residual levels, each having 256 trainable codewords, and emit exactly one global SID (k_i1,k_i2,k_i3) per item, shared across all users. No user input is accepted by Stage2. Stage3 T5 consumes these SIDs and ranks next items; Stage2 has no ranking objective or recommender component.
math_definition.assignment_and_losses: For item minibatch B, i in B, define q_il=argmin over j in {1,...,256} of d_c(P_c(exp0_c(r_il)),e_lj)^2 (lowest-index tie break), x_il=P_c(exp0_c(r_il)), a_il=invexp0_c(e_l,q_il), r_i1=z_i, and r_i,l+1=r_il-a_il. Stop-gradient through q_il. The per-item reconstruction and commitment objective is one equation: L_item=(1/|B|)*sum_{i in B}[||r_i4||_2^2+beta*sum_{l=1}^3 ||sg(r_il)-a_il||_2^2+gamma*sum_{l=1}^3 ||r_il-sg(a_il)||_2^2], with beta=0.25 and gamma=1.0; reductions are sums over latent dimensions and levels, then mean over items. The target code q_il is the argmin under current parameters but is treated as a stopped discrete index in the loss; the straight-through assignment estimator is used for the encoder path. Empty B is prohibited; an empty minibatch is skipped. All model, optimizer, epoch, batch, schedule, seed and initialization settings are inherited unchanged from the frozen Stage2 protocol, not tuned here.
math_definition.controls: Three runnable arms: (1) candidate hyperbolic geometry; (2) Euclidean metric control, identical architecture, parameter count, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, batch and budget, differing only by replacing every code-assignment distance with 4*||x-y||_2^2, using identity map, identity projection (no projection), and the corresponding identity residual chart; (3) graph-supervision control, same architecture, parameter count, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds and budget, trained with the train-split transition graph loss specified above, to distinguish a geometry effect from simply using graph signal. The graph arm is reported separately and does not replace the geometry-matched Euclidean comparison.

fixed_constants.arcosh_form: arcosh(u)=log(u+sqrt(max(u-1,0))*sqrt(u+1)); evaluate both square roots in float64 after clamping u to at least 1+1e-12, then cast the distance to the model dtype.
fixed_constants.domain_policy: The hyperbolic arm maps tangent vectors with exp0, then projects to the closed Poincare ball of radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c). Distances use the stated stable arcosh form and clamp the arcosh argument to at least 1+distance_clamp. The flat arm never applies this projection; its Euclidean vectors and codewords are unconstrained. No runtime-selected curvature or alternate domain policy is permitted.

math_definition.operations_and_geometry: Let exp0_c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)*||v||), with the ratio defined as 1 at zero; its c->0 limit is the identity. Let P_c(x)=x*min(1,((1-epsilon)/sqrt(c))/||x||), with scale 1 at zero. Its c->0 limit is undefined because the radius diverges; the flat arm instead applies the identity (no projection). For any residual r, each level performs exactly: map x=exp0_c(r); project xbar=P_c(x); assign k=argmin_j d_c(xbar,e_cj)^2 (ties choose lowest j); subtract r_next=r-invexp0_c(e_c,k), where invexp0_c(y)=atanh(sqrt(c)*||y||)*y/(sqrt(c)*||y||), ratio 1 at zero. The next residual is not projected or remapped until the next level. The squared distance is d_c(x,y)^2=[2/sqrt(c)*arcosh(1+2c*||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)*(1-c||y||^2)))]^2, using the fixed stable arcosh policy above. Its c->0 limit is 4*||x-y||^2. All codewords are constrained to the same ball after each optimizer update in the hyperbolic arm; the flat arm has no codeword projection.
math_definition.transition_auxiliary: The graph-control arm alone uses train-split directed transitions E={(i,j): i immediately precedes j in a user's train-split sequence}, with multiplicity w_ij equal to observed train-split count. Define s_i as the concatenation of the three selected code vectors a_i1,a_i2,a_i3, and p(j|i)=exp(-||s_i-s_j||_2^2/tau)/sum_{v in N(i)}exp(-||s_i-s_v||_2^2/tau), tau=1.0, N(i)={v:(i,v) in E}. The graph target distribution is one-hot t_ij=1[j is the observed successor], normalized over outgoing observed edges with multiplicity: t_ij=w_ij/sum_{v in N(i)}w_iv. Its loss is L_graph=-(1/|I_E|)*sum_{i in I_E}sum_{j in N(i)}t_ij*log p(j|i), where I_E={i: N(i) nonempty}; duplicate edges are represented by their counts. Empty I_E gives L_graph=0 and contributes no gradient. Targets depend only on frozen train-split transitions, never on learned parameters, so there is no target/parameter circularity. Total graph-arm objective is L_item+L_graph; the hyperbolic and Euclidean arms use L_item only. The graph arm is a supervision control, not the proposed candidate mechanism.

candidate.next_item_hypothesis: A single shared item SID can force distinct, semantically close items to share an early prefix. A downstream next-item model with a fixed user context may then be unable to express opposite preferences for those items. This candidate tests whether negatively curved residual code assignment separates such items into more discriminative prefixes; it does not claim that the supplied aggregate transition counts demonstrate rank reversals or establish a causal benefit.
candidate.real_trigger_measurement: The supplied train-only manifest measures directed transitions and next-item entropy, not rank reversals or code-prefix failures. Before interpreting a behavioral mechanism, measure on validation only whether distinct ground-truth next items that are close in content/code-prefix space exhibit user-specific preference rank reversals, using the fixed Stage3 evaluation procedure; do not use these measurements as Stage2 supervision or to alter the frozen protocol. The manifest's aggregate statistics alone do not establish this trigger.
candidate.training_only_inputs: Stage2 content embeddings and train-split item transitions only. Transitions are permitted supervision under CLAUDE.md rule 16, but are used only in the explicitly labeled graph control. No validation/test behavior, future events, prediction-time user context, or batch-composition signal may enter any training input, target, loss, code assignment or adaptation. Validation is used only for registered diagnostics; test is used only for the registered Stage3 behavioral test.
